history.summary: Bhabani (Bhawani) Pathak was a legendary leader of the Fakir-Sanyasi rebellion against the East India Company in late-18th-century Bengal, immortalised by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in the novels 'Devi Chaudhurani' and 'Durgeshnandini'. Local lore says the small Kali temple on this mound (tilla) by the Damodar, near Durgapur's City Centre, was where Pathak worshipped the goddess before his dacoity expeditions, and that a tunnel ran from the mound to the Damodar's banks (now closed by the government; the site is now the Devi Chaudhurani-Bhabani Pathak Tunnel Park). Visitor reviews describe the temple premises as neat, tranquil and locally frequented, with a friendly priest. A reviewer claim that this is Durgapur's oldest Kali temple is unverified. The CSV town Durgapur is correct.

name: Bhabani Pathak's Tilla Temple
town_description: Durgapur is a major industrial city on the Damodar river in Paschim Bardhaman district, conceived under Dr B.C. Roy's plan as a steel township and home to the Durgapur Steel Plant. It is the fourth-largest urban agglomeration of West Bengal, combining heavy industry and residential townships with scattered historic remains such as the Bhabani Pathak Tilla.

travel.airport: Kazi Nazrul Islam Airport, Andal (~25 km) (verify); Kolkata's NSCB airport is the major alternative
travel.railway: Durgapur station (Howrah-Delhi main line); auto-rickshaw from the station to City Centre costs only a few tens of rupees
travel.road: NH-19 passes through Durgapur; ~170 km from Kolkata by road

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; early morning for the tunnel park
visitor_information.opening_hours: Tunnel park gates 10 AM-6 PM (travel guide); temple hours not published - verify locally
